title: Proliferation Financing Networks and Dual-Use Goods Red Flags
summary: How proliferation networks procure weapons-related and dual-use goods, conceal their activity through front companies, shipping and intermediaries, and the red flags that may surface in a firm's customers and payments.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How proliferation networks procure weapons-related and dual-use goods, conceal their activity through front companies, shipping and intermediaries, and the red flags that may surface in a firm's customers and payments.
Learning Objectives: Explain how procurement networks source goods and move funds
Recognise dual-use goods, trade and corporate red flags
Apply enhanced due diligence to customers with trade or technology exposure
Syllabus: Procurement networks, front companies and third-country diversion
Dual-use goods, end-user and routing red flags in payments and invoices
Exposure through investors, portfolio companies, payment flows and crypto-assets
Enhanced due diligence on technology, logistics and trading customers
Intended Audience: MLROs, compliance officers and financial crime analysts in investment, fund, payment, crypto-asset and fintech firms
Sanctions and screening teams responsible for customer, investor and payment screening
Senior managers and risk owners for products, corridors or customer segments with terrorist or proliferation financing exposure
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of AML/CFT compliance or sanctions screening is helpful. No prior specialist knowledge of terrorist or proliferation financing is required.
Core Reading: FATF, International Standards on Combating Money Laundering and the Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation: The FATF Recommendations (as updated)
FATF, Terrorist Financing Risk Assessment Guidance (2019)
FATF, Guidance on Proliferation Financing Risk Assessment and Mitigation (2021)
FATF, Best Practices on Combating the Abuse of Non-Profit Organisations (2023)
